summary: Recorded the staleleader receipt and closed the leader-side half of the open applicability question. Receipt dda5bb4179154e3abe90e69f5267b3ea (all four tests passed) reproduced the earlier witnesses and showed that the node which took over from a follower whose Promise carried the StopSign was itself inflated: accepted index 7 over its six indices of content, read(5) returning None and a one-element decided-log read (event 13), with both other nodes ending at accepted 7 and a one-element read (events 12, 14), so the corruption propagates across the authority change; declared comparisons 7-10 on that leader were violated at index 13, the newterm reproduction at index 11, and the baselines and the untouched nodes held. Updates: the interpretation now covers all four receipts separately with same-run controls and joint_history (violated/asserted) and records that the trigger is a resume point covering the StopSign rather than the reconnection API; the applicability fact lists the third observed producer instance (a candidate leader syncing from a follower via handle_majority_promises); a new behavior records that candidate-leader path; the answer to the open gap states the leader half as witnessed and the snapshot half as still sourced-only; and a successor experiment is submitted that adds a snapshot-capable entry type (Snapshot::use_snapshots() true) and repeats the two-follower reconnection after a decided StopSign, with baseline comparisons on the StopSign index, the six-element decided read and the endpoint, and result comparisons requiring the re-synchronized replicas and the leader to keep them. Incomplete: the snapshot-enabled execution, loss- and timer-triggered re-synchronization, larger clusters, persistence across restarts, and any independent second defect lead.
